膜.meaning: At <part>sunset</part>, a girl blows a soap bubble so big it floats up and wraps the rising <part>moon</part>. For one night the moon wears a shimmering skin, thin as cling film, wobbling in every breeze. Astronomers call it the thinnest <kanji>membrane</kanji> in the sky.
膜.on: When it pops, a splash of soapy <sound>muck</sound> rains down on her garden.

眺.meaning: A fortune teller cracks an old turtle shell to read a <part>portent</part>, and the cracks seem to say: 'Blink and you'll miss it.' So she doesn't blink. One wide <part>eye</part> stays fixed on the shell all night. At dawn the cracks spell 'joke'. She had to <kanji>stare</kanji> for nothing.
眺.on: Her tight pearl <sound>cho</sound>ker glints as she leans in closer.
眺.kun: For breakfast she eats <sound>na</sound>an with <sound>ga</sound>rlic, still gazing at the shell.

顧.meaning: A bank decides to <part>employ</part> a <part>rubber duck</part> as head of security. It floats in the lobby fountain and slowly spins round all day, so it always sees who's behind it. Thieves give up at once. Nobody is better at turning to <kanji>look back</kanji>.
顧.on: Its deputy is a sleepy <sound>ko</sound>ala who watches the door.
顧.kun: In the fountain with it float a <sound>ca</sound>rp, a plastic <sound>e</sound>gg and a chunk of coral <sound>ree</sound>f.

陶.meaning: A toddler keeps her toys in an old <part>tin can</part>. Her grandmother, a potter, secretly coats it in clay, folds a damp cloth <part>wrap</part> round it to dry, then fires it in the kiln. Out comes a glazed jar with a tiny <part>pennant</part> painted on the lid. Even the toy box is <kanji>pottery</kanji> now.
陶.on: The toddler taps it with one bare <sound>toe</sound>, and it rings like a bell.
陶.kun: Inside she finds a <sound>su</sound>shi roll and a painted <sound>e</sound>gg.

肢.meaning: A wooden puppet has lost an arm. The puppeteer climbs a tree by the light of the <part>moon</part>, snaps off a thin <part>branch</part> with twigs for fingers and screws it on. The puppet waves it and tickles the cat. One new <kanji>limb</kanji>, fresh from the tree.
肢.on: The puppet celebrates by waving a tiny wooden <sound>shi</sound>eld.

漏.meaning: A proud king sleeps under his royal <part>flag</part> instead of a roof. When the <part>rain</part> starts, <part>water drops</part> seep through the stitched lion and fall, plip, plip, into the royal ear. By dawn he's floating on his mattress. Every flag has a <kanji>leak</kanji>.
漏.on: He drifts out of the door clutching a red <sound>ro</sound>se.
漏.kun: The servants run in with a <sound>mo</sound>p, and a soggy <sound>roo</sound>k shakes itself dry on the bedpost.

敢.meaning: A tiny mouse climbs the high <part>diving board</part> at the pool, holding a paper <part>fan</part> as a parachute. Everyone covers one <part>ear</part> and squints. It jumps, flutters and lands right on the lifeguard's whistle. Nobody has ever seen anything so <kanji>daring</kanji>.
敢.on: The lifeguard pins a pink <sound>car</sound>nation to its tiny chest.
敢.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the crowd, and the mouse is fed boiled <sound>e</sound>gg in a little <sound>te</sound>nt by the pool.

侍.meaning: At a mountain <part>temple</part>, a tired traveller hangs his cloak on the <part>coat hook</part> by the door. A second later a silent man in a white apron appears with tea, rice and a hot towel, then vanishes. Even the monks don't know where he hides. He's the fastest <kanji>waiter</kanji> in the hills.
侍.on: He takes noodles to the far huts in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p.
侍.kun: His apron pocket holds a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and a toy <sound>moo</sound>se; when he bows, the monks cheer '<sound>Rah</sound>!' and he serves them grilled <sound>ee</sound>l.

翻.meaning: At a pancake contest, each cook waits for their <part>turn</part>. A goose steps up and tosses the pan with one wing. The pancake spins away and lands on her head like a hat, with <part>feathers</part> stuck all over it. The crowd roars. She wins first prize for the best <kanji>flip</kanji>.
翻.on: The judge sounds a <sound>hon</sound>king horn to announce her win.
翻.kun: Her prize basket holds a shoe with a tall <sound>hee</sound>l, a toy <sound>roo</sound>k, a clove of <sound>ga</sound>rlic and one golden <sound>e</sound>gg.

瀬.meaning: A blind otter guides rafting trips through the roughest stretch of river. The passengers must <part>trust</part> her completely as <part>water drops</part> fly and the raft bucks like a horse. She steers by sound alone and never hits a rock. Nobody else dares run these <kanji>rapids</kanji>.
瀬.on: On the bank, a <sound>rhi</sound>no cheers every raft that makes it through.
瀬.kun: Where the shallows begin, a red <sound>se</sound>tter splashes out to fetch the lost paddle.

飽.meaning: A squirrel finds a picnic and eats every crumb of <part>food</part> in sight. Then she tries to <part>pack up</part> the leftovers in her cheeks for winter, but there's no room: too full to chew, too full to climb, too full to care. She just lies on the blanket, <kanji>sated</kanji>.
飽.on: A boy cools her round belly with a gentle spray from the garden <sound>ho</sound>se.
飽.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>,' she sighs, pushing away the last acorn: tired of it.

舗.meaning: Under a big striped <part>umbrella</part>, a little old man sells only one thing: a <part>flyswatter</part> with a <part>good luck</part> charm painted on the handle. He swears they make buses come on time. The queue goes round the block. It's the busiest <kanji>shop</kanji> in town.
舗.on: People waiting in line munch a <sound>ho</sound>tdog from the stall next door.

鏡.meaning: A <part>bellhop</part> at a grand hotel polishes the <part>gold</part> frame in the lobby every morning. One day he winks, and his reflection doesn't. It takes his cap and strolls off to the lift. Now he carries the bags, and his double works the <kanji>mirror</kanji>.
鏡.on: A guest asks the double where it learned such manners; it bows and says '<sound>Kyo</sound>to', stretching the start out long.
鏡.kun: On its break the double eats a <sound>ca</sound>rp with <sound>ga</sound>rlic, while a <sound>mee</sound>rkat peeks out from behind the frame.

雄.meaning: A tiny <part>sparrow</part> perches on a weightlifter's <part>bent arm</part> while he flexes in front of the gym mirror. The sparrow puffs up its chest, spreads its wings and struts along the bicep. Two show-offs, one arm. Each thinks he's the most <kanji>masculine</kanji> thing in the room.
雄.on: Then a <sound>u</sound>nicorn trots in and lifts the whole bench with its horn.
雄.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the sparrow, and drops its <sound>su</sound>shi.

朗.meaning: A <part>good</part> old shepherd sits on the hill each night and sings to the full <part>moon</part>, his voice like warm honey. Neighbours open their windows, owls stop hooting to listen, and even the moon seems to sway. No voice in the valley is so <kanji>melodious</kanji>.
朗.on: He throws a red <sound>ro</sound>se up to the moon at the end of every song.
朗.kun: His sheep share his supper, all smiles: a <sound>ho</sound>tdog with extra <sound>ga</sound>rlic.

炊.meaning: On a camping trip, a lazy dragon is told to make the rice. It can't be bothered to light a <part>fire</part>, so it lets out a huge <part>yawn</part> over the pot. A puff of flame, a hiss of steam, and the rice is perfect. That's how a dragon likes to <kanji>cook</kanji>.
炊.on: For pudding it yawns over a pan of sugar and makes a <sound>swee</sound>t.
炊.kun: Then it warms a <sound>tu</sound>b of bathwater for the camp <sound>coo</sound>k.

径.meaning: A <part>tumbleweed</part> blows into a ski resort and gets stuck on the <part>chairlift</part>. Up it goes, so wide it scrapes both poles. The engineer climbs up and runs a tape measure straight across its middle: two metres exactly. He writes down its <kanji>diameter</kanji>.
径.on: He celebrates with a round birthday <sound>ca</sound>ke, and measures that too.
径.kun: Below, a <sound>mee</sound>rkat and a <sound>chee</sound>tah race down the ski trail after it: the path.

霊.meaning: At a birthday party in a storm, the <part>rain</part> blows in and puts out every light except <part>one</part> row of <part>candles</part>, which relight by themselves. Nobody at the table blew on them. A chair at the end slides back, and the cake has a slice missing. The house <kanji>spirits</kanji> came too.
霊.on: Outside in the flooded street, a glowing <sound>ray</sound> glides past, carrying the missing slice.
霊.kun: Later, someone unseen runs a hot <sound>tu</sound>b and leaves a <sound>mu</sound>g of cocoa steaming beside it.

慰.meaning: A gruff <part>jailer</part> hears a prisoner crying over a lost game of chess. He unlocks nothing, but slides a chocolate <part>heart</part> through the bars and sits down to lose the next game on purpose. The prisoner grins. Not freedom, but a fine <kanji>consolation</kanji>.
慰.on: Next night the jailer brings a smoked <sound>ee</sound>l for supper.
慰.kun: He also hands over warm <sound>na</sound>an, a <sound>goo</sound>die bag and a <sound>sa</sound>rdine for the prison cat.

鉢.meaning: A dragon who hoards <part>gold</part> reads a cookery <part>book</part> and decides coins are useless for soup. He melts a heap of them into one deep round dish, big enough to bathe in, and stirs his stew with his tail. The treasure is gone, but he has a lovely <kanji>bowl</kanji>.
鉢.on: He carries it to his <sound>hu</sound>t and shares the stew with a hungry <sound>chee</sound>tah.

誉.meaning: A shy goat with little <part>horns</part> gives <part>one</part> short <part>speech</part> at the village fair: 'Thank you for the hay.' The crowd goes wild, a <part>sparkle</part> of camera flashes fills the air, and by morning every paper calls him wise. One sentence built his <kanji>reputation</kanji>.
誉.on: Fans send him pot after pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt with fan letters.
誉.kun: At his parties he serves a <sound>ho</sound>tdog in a <sound>mu</sound>g with <sound>re</sound>d sauce.

瓦.meaning: A roofer has <part>one</part> piece left to finish the temple roof. A gust snatches it, and it skims across the pond like a stone, ten hops, before landing neatly on a turtle's back. The turtle now wears a curved clay <kanji>tile</kanji> and won't give it back.
瓦.on: The roofer offers the turtle a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic in exchange.
瓦.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>rp in the pond gasps, '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and the frogs cheer, '<sound>Rah</sound>!'

瓶.meaning: A glassblower makes a pair of glass <part>rugby posts</part> for a contest, then notices they look like a neck and shoulders. She melts them together onto a clay <part>tile</part> base, puffs, and pops a cork in the top. Out comes the shiniest <kanji>bottle</kanji> at the fair.
瓶.on: The judge drops it in the recycling <sound>bin</sound> by mistake.
瓶.kun: She fishes it out and fills it with a baby <sound>ca</sound>rp and a slice of <sound>me</sound>lon.

忙.meaning: A stonemason has a hundred orders due by Friday. She carves one little <part>tombstone</part> after another for the garden gnome museum, chisel flying, her <part>heartbeat</part> pounding like a drum. No lunch, no tea, no sitting down. She's never been so <kanji>busy</kanji>.
忙.on: Then a lorry tips out a whole <sound>bou</sound>lder for the next one.
忙.kun: She eats a smoked <sound>ee</sound>l standing up, ignores the <sound>so</sound>fa, and chews <sound>ga</sound>rlic to stay awake.

尋.meaning: A golfer loses her ball in a garden. She leans her <part>golf club</part> on the gardener's <part>workbench</part>, borrows his <part>rake</part> and combs every flowerbed. At last she cups her <part>mouth</part> and calls to the hedgehog curled in the roses: 'Seen a small white ball?' It's polite to <kanji>inquire</kanji>.
尋.on: The hedgehog is busy grating <sound>gin</sound>ger for his tea and doesn't look up.
尋.kun: She finds the ball at last in a <sound>tu</sound>b of rainwater, bobbing next to a yu<sound>zu</sound>.

粛.meaning: In a silent temple hall, a monk drags a wet <part>mop</part> across the floor without a sound. A single <part>slash</part> of light falls through the window onto a bowl of <part>rice</part>. Nobody coughs, nobody smiles, and even the mouse tiptoes. The whole hall is <kanji>solemn</kanji>.
粛.on: The mouse nibbles a <sound>su</sound>gar <sound>cu</sound>be in total silence.
粛.kun: It nearly sneezes, '<sound>Tsu</sound>, <sound>tsu</sound>...', then buries its nose in a <sound>shee</sound>p's wool: restraint.

獄.meaning: A <part>dog</part> sits behind bars, howling a long <part>speech</part> about how he never stole the sausages. Then a <part>fishhook</part> on a string dangles through the window. He grabs it, climbs out and leaves one sausage behind as a thank-you. Nothing can keep him in <kanji>prison</kanji>.
獄.on: He runs off wearing swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles, humming like a <sound>cu</sound>ckoo clock.

紹.meaning: At a big party, nobody knows anyone. A tailor ties a <part>thread</part> from each guest's button to a stranger's, then makes a loud <part>call</part>: 'Follow your string!' Everyone ends up face to face with someone new and has to say hello. That's his way to <kanji>introduce</kanji> people.
紹.on: Soon the whole tangled party is putting on a <sound>show</sound> together.

縫.meaning: A soldier in a <part>lookout post</part> on a hill rips his trousers. Bored, he lowers a <part>thread</part> down the long <part>ramp</part> to his grandmother at the bottom, who ties a needle to it. He hauls it up and spends the whole night watch learning to <kanji>sew</kanji>.
縫.on: Next she sends up a garden <sound>ho</sound>se, so he can water the flowers on the roof.
縫.kun: He sits in a quiet <sound>noo</sound>k of the tower, stitching.

窮.meaning: A hunter is so broke he lives in a <part>hole</part> in the hillside. His <part>pot belly</part> has shrunk flat, and he has sold everything but his old <part>bow</part>, which he plays like a fiddle for coins. A rabbit drops him a carrot out of pity. He's truly <kanji>hard up</kanji>.
窮.on: He even swaps his last arrow for a broken pool <sound>cue</sound>.
窮.kun: Then he digs up a rusty <sound>key</sound> and cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!': it opens a treasure chest at last, the very end of his bad luck.
